features.name: Host Connection Fails With DNS Error On Valid IP (Invisible Characters In Hostname)
features.description: User on Xiaomi Redmi Note 8 Pro (Android 15) reports SSH connection to host 'arch' (192.168.50.45) fails immediately with a DNS resolution error, even though 192.168.50.45 is a syntactically valid IPv4 literal that should never trigger DNS. Log (darkssh_20260716_233139.log) shows: 'SSH: Connecting to 192.168.50.45:22' followed by 'java.net.UnknownHostException: Unable to resolve host "192.168.50.45": No address associated with hostname' caused by 'android.system.GaiException: EAI_NODATA'. Root cause: java.net.InetAddress.getAllByName() only skips DNS when its strict IPv4-literal parser (IPAddressUtil.textToNumericFormatV4, exact match against digits+dots) recognizes the string; ANY extra character - a trailing/leading space, a non-breaking space, a zero-width space/BOM inserted by mobile keyboard autocomplete/autocorrect or paste - makes it fall through to a real DNS lookup, which then fails because the corrupted string isn't a resolvable hostname either. Confirmed nowhere in the Host save path (HostEditorScreen.kt hostname OutlinedTextField -> HostEditorViewModel.saveHost() -> Host entity) or in SSH.kt connect() does any .trim() or sanitization happen on nickname/hostname/username.
features.evidence:
Root cause confirmed by log analysis (darkssh_20260716_233139.log, provided by user from their Xiaomi Redmi Note 8 Pro / Android 15 device): SSH.connect() logged 'Connecting to 192.168.50.45:22' then immediately threw java.net.UnknownHostException: 'Unable to resolve host "192.168.50.45": No address associated with hostname' caused by android.system.GaiException EAI_NODATA - i.e. Android tried a real DNS lookup on a syntactically valid IPv4 literal, which only happens when java.net.InetAddress's strict IPv4-literal parser fails to match the string exactly (any extra invisible character defeats it). Confirmed no .trim()/sanitization existed anywhere in the Host save path (HostEditorScreen.kt -> HostEditorViewModel.saveHost() -> Host entity) or in SSH.kt connect()/authenticate(). Fix: (1) new util/TextSanitizer.kt - trims regular whitespace then strips a set of invisible Unicode chars (BOM \uFEFF, zero-width space \u200B, ZWNJ \u200C, ZWJ \u200D, word joiner \u2060, non-breaking space \u00A0) by scanning the WHOLE string, not just the edges, since java.lang.Character.isWhitespace() (used by Kotlin's String.trim()) deliberately does NOT treat \u00A0/\u2007/\u202F as whitespace - a plain .trim() alone would miss a trailing NBSP. (2) HostEditorViewModel.saveHost() now sanitizes nickname/hostname/username before persisting (both insert and update paths), keeping the DB clean going forward. (3) SSH.kt connect() and authenticate() also sanitize host.hostname/host.username at use-time, independently of save-time, so the user's ALREADY-BROKEN 'arch' host (hostId=1, saved before this fix) is unblocked immediately once the new APK is installed - no need to re-open Host Editor and retype the hostname. Verified: ./gradlew clean assembleDebug BUILD SUCCESSFUL (44/44 fresh tasks) + ./init.sh BUILD SUCCESSFUL. Not yet verified against the actual corrupted DB row on the user's Xiaomi device (no adb access to that device in this session, only the log file was provided) - user should reinstall the new APK and retry connecting to 'arch' without editing the host, then report back.

--- UPDATE (round 2, same session) ---
User reinstalled the APK with the round-1 fix and reported it did NOT work: fresh log showed the exact same UnknownHostException/EAI_NODATA for host id=1 'arch' (192.168.50.45), with the SSH.kt line number shifted (confirming the new sanitize-at-connect code WAS running) - meaning the round-1 blacklist (BOM, ZWSP, ZWNJ, ZWJ, word joiner, NBSP) did not contain whatever character actually corrupted that host's hostname. User worked around it by deleting the host and recreating it with the same IP, which connected successfully (proving the save-time path, going through the same TextSanitizer, DID produce a clean string when the user retyped it - so the theory was right, the character list just wasn't complete).
Root-caused without device access via a throwaway javac/java test (/tmp/opencode/chartest/Test.java, Test2.java): confirmed 17 different single-character insertions around a valid IPv4 literal (NBSP, ZWSP, ZWNJ, ZWJ, BOM, word joiner, LRM, RLM, soft hyphen, line separator, paragraph separator, ideographic space, emoji variation selector FE0F, tab, LF, CR, even plain ASCII space) ALL reproduce the identical UnknownHostException/EAI_NODATA failure against java.net.InetAddress - confirming a hand-picked blacklist can never be complete for this class of bug.
Replaced the blacklist with two functions in TextSanitizer.kt: sanitize() (light - trims, strips characters by Unicode general category CONTROL/FORMAT/LINE_SEPARATOR/PARAGRAPH_SEPARATOR, normalizes any other SPACE_SEPARATOR variant like NBSP/ideographic-space to a real ' ' instead of dropping it so words don't glue together - used for nickname/username, which can legitimately contain spaces) and sanitizeStrict() (sanitize() + a hostname/IP whitelist regex [^A-Za-z0-9.\-:_\[\]] that strips anything else - used for hostname only, which never legitimately contains anything outside that charset). HostEditorViewModel.saveHost() and SSH.kt connect() both now call sanitizeStrict() for hostname (was sanitize()); username/nickname keep the light sanitize(). Verified with the same javac/java harness: sanitizeStrict() reduces ALL 17 corrupted variants back to the exact clean IP string, 0 failures (was passing only 6/17 with the round-1 blacklist). Verified: ./gradlew clean assembleDebug BUILD SUCCESSFUL (44/44 fresh) + ./init.sh BUILD SUCCESSFUL. Still not confirmed against the user's live device (they already deleted the broken host, so there's no remaining corrupted row to retest against) - confidence now comes from exhaustive local JVM testing of the actual failure mode, not from a single anecdotal device retry.

features.name: sshj Removed — cbssh Is the Only SFTP Backend (migrate-sftp-to-cbssh Phases 5-7 complete)
features.description: Closed the remaining gaps for SFTP auth parity (host-key verification, key-based auth), fixed real-device performance/UX bugs found via dogfooding (Ed25519 detection on Android/Conscrypt, misleading copy-paste progress UI, upload having zero pipelining, an adaptive-pipeline self-congestion bug), then removed sshj and its feature flag entirely once real-device testing confirmed parity + meaningfully better throughput.
features.evidence: Real device: Xiaomi 25069PTEBG, Android 16. (1) DarkSshHostKeyVerifier.kt: real TOFU host-key verification for SftpClient2 (was hardcoded always-trust); SftpViewModel wired to always use connectWithKey for pubkeyId-assigned hosts, matching SSH.kt's terminal behavior. (2) KeyPairToPem.kt: Ed25519 key-type detection fixed via RFC 8410 OID-byte sniffing (DER `06 03 2B 65 70`) instead of algorithm-name matching — Android/Conscrypt's OpenSslEdDsaPrivateKey.getAlgorithm() doesn't return a recognizable 'Ed25519'/'EdDSA' string, confirmed by 2 failed attempts before the OID fix; same bug independently confirmed present in sshj's own KeyType.fromKey() via javap on the 0.38.0 jar (`"EdDSA".equals(key.getAlgorithm())`), making an sshj-vs-cbssh key-auth A/B comparison impossible and giving extra confidence sshj wasn't worth keeping around. (3) SftpViewModel.pasteFiles(): stopped fabricating a byte-shaped TransferProgress from a file COUNT for server-side cp/mv (was stuck showing '0 B / 1 B' for a whole large-file copy, looking hung); now passes progress=null so the UI's existing indeterminate spinner renders instead, with per-file status conveyed via a new updateTransferLabel() helper. (4) TransferEngine.uploadInternal: was 100% serial (write chunk → await full ack → next chunk), capping throughput at chunkSize/RTT regardless of bandwidth; pipelined it with a sliding window of in-flight writes (PipelineWriteRequest + retryWriteChunk), mirroring the download path's existing design. (5) Real-device log (375MB LAN transfer) showed TransferEngine's adaptive pipeline pinned at max depth while its own measured avgRtt climbed into the seconds/tens-of-seconds — a runaway self-congestion loop with no backoff. Added a panicRttMs circuit breaker (default 2000ms) that snaps depth straight to minPipelineDepth instead of a gradual ±1 crawl; also lowered maxPipelineDepth 32→16 after confirming the breaker still fired repeatedly at 32. Retested on the same 375MB file/host: download 856KB/s→1512KB/s (+77%), upload 676KB/s→3227KB/s (+377%). (6) Ruled out re-litigating the earlier SSH-channel-window-size fix (fork commit 49af22a, 16MB window) via javap on the actual .m2 jar — confirmed compiled in and in use, not the cause of the perf issue. (7) With functional parity + performance verified, deleted SftpClient.kt (sshj), SftpClientFactory.kt, the useCbsshSftp preference + Settings toggle, and the com.hierynomus:sshj Gradle dependency; SftpClient2 (cbssh) is now the only ISftpClient implementation. APK size: 56.07MB→52.07MB debug (-4.0MB). ./init.sh green throughout (92/92 unit tests after removal, was 95 before — 3 removed tests covered the now-gone sshj/cbssh branching), assembleDebug builds, 7 pre-existing Docker integration tests unaffected. openspec: cbssh-migration-strategy 16/21 tasks (remaining 5 are Docker-only follow-ups); migrate-sftp-to-cbssh reached Phases 1-6 done and was archived as 2026-07-23-migrate-sftp-to-cbssh, alongside archiving the now-superseded refactor-sftp-client-sshj spec.

features.name: SFTP Copy/Cut Appear Broken — Paste Button Never Shows Up
features.description: User reports 'copiar y cortar no funcionan' (copy and cut don't work) in the SFTP file browser. Tapping Copy/Cut on a file shows a confirmation snackbar but the Paste toolbar icon never appears, so pasted files can't actually be placed anywhere — the operation looks completely non-functional even though the underlying data is captured correctly.
features.evidence: Root cause found via static code analysis (no device logs needed): SftpClipboard (app/src/main/java/com/darkssh/client/ui/screens/viewmodel/SftpClipboard.kt) stored its ClipboardData in a plain Kotlin `var data: ClipboardData? = null` inside a singleton object — not a Compose snapshot State. SftpScreen.kt's SftpActions() composable gates the Paste IconButton on `if (viewModel.hasClipboardData())`, and SftpViewModel.hasClipboardData()/getClipboardOperation()/getClipboardFileCount() are plain passthrough functions reading that var directly. Compose's recomposition system only reacts to snapshot-state reads (mutableStateOf, StateFlow.collectAsState, etc.) inside a tracked scope; a bare `var` mutation on a singleton object is invisible to it. So copyFiles()/cutFiles() correctly wrote to SftpClipboard.data (confirmed by re-reading the code and by the snackbar firing, which uses an independent coroutine/SnackbarHostState path unrelated to Compose state), but SftpActions() never recomposed to reflect it — the Paste icon stayed hidden until some UNRELATED recomposition happened to fire (e.g. navigating to a different folder), which is why it looked totally broken to the user. Confirmed the reverse case (successful paste) worked 'by accident' only because pasteFiles()'s completion handler additionally does `_uiState.value = _uiState.value.copy(message=...)`, a real StateFlow update, coinciding with SftpClipboard.clear(). Fix: changed `private var data: ClipboardData? = null` to `private var data: ClipboardData? by mutableStateOf(null)` (androidx.compose.runtime) in SftpClipboard.kt — minimal, localized fix that makes the existing singleton properly observable without restructuring it into the ViewModel's StateFlow/uiState. Verified: ./init.sh BUILD SUCCESSFUL (all unit tests pass), ./gradlew assembleDebug BUILD SUCCESSFUL. Not yet re-tested on a physical device by the user (code-only fix, no device log was provided for this report).

features.name: SFTP Paste Hangs Forever Showing 'Copiando' / 'Moviendo' (Never Times Out)
features.description: Follow-up to bug-014: the user clarified that the actual reported problem is not the missing Paste button, but that tapping Paste on a Copy'd or Cut file shows the 'Copiando'/'Moviendo' progress indicator and never completes, hanging indefinitely with no error and no way out.
features.evidence: Root cause: SftpClient2.copyFileViaSsh (used for paste-after-Copy) and deleteDirectoryViaSsh (used for delete) run `cp`/`rm -rf` server-side via a raw SSH exec session, then drain stdout with `while (true) { s.read() ?: break }` — a suspend function reading a Kotlin Channel with NO timeout. If the remote command never sends CHANNEL_EOF (e.g. a `cp`/`rm` shell alias like `alias cp='cp -i'` silently waiting on an interactive overwrite confirmation on stdin that is never sent, a wedged remote shell, or any other reason the process doesn't exit), that `read()` suspends forever with no exception — exactly matching the reported symptom. This exact failure mode was already flagged as a known gap in a pre-existing backlog TODO (id 220, added 2026-07-22: 'SftpClient2.copyFileViaSsh no tiene timeout... considerar timeout razonable configurable para abortar automáticamente si el servidor se cuelga'). Ruled out a stderr-backpressure deadlock theory (remote process blocking on a full stderr pipe because only stdout was drained) by reading cbssh-fork's LocalChannelWindow.consumeLocal(), which immediately replenishes the local SSH flow-control window as soon as any data arrives over the wire, regardless of whether the app has actually called read() yet — so the SSH protocol itself never backpressures the server this way in this implementation. Could not reproduce with device logs for this specific report, so the exact trigger (interactive alias vs. a genuinely wedged server vs. something else) is unconfirmed, but a bounded timeout with a clear error message is the correct, low-risk mitigation regardless: it turns a silent infinite hang into a recoverable failure within at most 120s. Fix (SftpClient2.kt): added `internal var execCommandTimeoutMs` set to a 120s default (renamed from an inline private const, matching the existing `useTransferEngine` companion-var pattern so a future test can override it), wrapped the stdout-drain loop in `withTimeout(execCommandTimeoutMs) { ... }` in copyFileViaSsh, deleteDirectoryViaSsh, and executeCommand (the third is currently dead code but fixed for consistency/future use), catching TimeoutCancellationException specifically to return a clear Result.failure instead of hanging. Also added `catch (e: CancellationException) { throw e }` before the existing generic `catch (e: Exception)` in all three functions — the pre-existing generic catch was ALSO swallowing a real user-initiated cancellation (tapping Cancel on the transfer), not just our new TimeoutCancellationException, mirroring the exact pattern already fixed for CbsshTransfer in bug-013. Verified: ./init.sh BUILD SUCCESSFUL (unit tests pass), ./gradlew assembleDebug BUILD SUCCESSFUL. Not yet verified on a physical device against a real hang repro (no device log was available for this report) — added a medium-priority TODO for a Docker-integration-test that forces a slow remote command (`execCommandTimeoutMs` overridden small + `sleep 5`) to verify the timeout path end-to-end; blocked on needing a mocked KnownHostRepository + likely Robolectric since DarkSshHostKeyVerifier.verify() calls android.util.Base64 unconditionally.

features.name: Native SFTP Server-Side Copy via OpenSSH 'copy-data' Extension (Replaces exec `cp` as Primary Path)
features.description: Follow-up to bug-015: instead of only mitigating the exec-based `cp` hang with a timeout, implement the modern/standard mechanism for server-side SFTP copy — the OpenSSH 'copy-data' protocol extension (SSH_FXP_EXTENDED) — in cbssh-fork, and wire SftpClient2.copyFileViaSsh to prefer it whenever the server advertises support, falling back to the (now timeout-bounded) exec `cp` only for servers that don't.
features.evidence:
Root cause of preferring this over exec: SFTP v3 (the protocol OpenSSH implements) has no COPY operation in its base message set (OPEN/READ/WRITE/CLOSE/RENAME/REMOVE/MKDIR/etc. only) — the standard extension mechanism for this is SSH_FXP_EXTENDED (type 200), and OpenSSH 9.0+ (April 2022) defines the 'copy-data' extension exactly for server-side copy between two open file handles, entirely on the server (e.g. via copy_file_range() on Linux), no shell/exec involved at all — works even for accounts restricted to internal-sftp with no shell, where exec-based cp cannot run at all.

cbssh-fork changes (org.connectbot.sshlib 0.3.2-SNAPSHOT -> 0.3.3-SNAPSHOT, published to mavenLocal): (1) SftpClientImpl.create() now parses the extension-name/extension-data string pairs that trail the SSH_FXP_VERSION handshake reply (previously completely ignored — only the 4-byte version int was read), defensively (a malformed trailing pair just stops parsing rather than failing the whole handshake). (2) New SftpClient.extensions: Set<String> property exposing the parsed names. (3) New SftpClient.copyData(srcHandle, srcOffset, length, dstHandle, dstOffset): SftpResult<Unit> sending the 'copy-data' SSH_FXP_EXTENDED request (both handles must already be open by the caller; length=0 means 'through EOF'). (4) sshlib/api.txt regenerated via metalava. (5) Tests: SftpClientImplTest — 4 new unit tests (extension-pair parsing with/without extensions present, copyData wire-payload correctness, OP_UNSUPPORTED error mapping) using the file's existing FakeSshSession harness, no Docker needed. SftpClientIntegrationTest — 2 new Docker tests against a REAL OpenSSH 9.9p2 server (Testcontainers): confirms the server actually advertises 'copy-data' in its real VERSION reply (validates the parsing against real wire bytes, not just hand-built test payloads), and confirms copyData() actually copies bytes correctly server-side (write source, copyData, read destination, byte-for-byte match). Full `:sshlib:test` suite (all SSH/SFTP/port-forwarding/compat Docker tests) still green after the change.

clientssh changes (SftpClient2.kt): copyFileViaSsh now checks `EXT_COPY_DATA in client.extensions` first; if present, tries copyDataSingleFile (open src READ + dst WRITE/CREATE/(TRUNCATE|EXCLUDE per overwrite flag), copyData, close both) for a single file, or copyDataRecursive (mkdir dest, listdir source, recurse per subdirectory / copyDataSingleFile per regular file — there's no protocol-level 'copy whole directory' operation, copy-data only copies bytes between two already-open regular files, so the client has to drive the tree walk) for isDirectory=true. The previous exec-based implementation was renamed to copyFileViaExec (private) and kept verbatim (including its bug-015 timeout) as the fallback for servers that don't advertise the extension, or if the native path throws/fails unexpectedly for any other reason (defensive fall-through, not just a hard dependency on the new path). Verified: confirmed the actual test-container image clientssh's own Docker integration tests use (linuxserver/openssh-server:latest, Alpine 3.24) runs OpenSSH 10.3p1 — well above the 9.0 minimum — so the native path is exercised, not silently skipped, in this repo's own test environment too. ./init.sh BUILD SUCCESSFUL (unit tests green), ./gradlew assembleDebug BUILD SUCCESSFUL with the new cbssh 0.3.3-SNAPSHOT dependency. Not yet verified end-to-end at the SftpClient2 level with a Docker test (blocked on the same KnownHostRepository-mock/Robolectric gap as bug-015's own follow-up TODO — logged a new TODO to cover both together) nor on a physical device — recommend the user retest Copy+Paste on their device to confirm the native path resolves the original hang. | Fork listo para PR: rama feat/copy-data-extension rebasada sobre upstream/main (372c1cb), api.txt limpio (solo copy-data, sin contaminación keepAlive), spotless OK, metalavaCheckCompatibility OK, 1215 tests 0 fallos (incl. SftpClientImplTest 19, SftpClientIntegrationTest 14 con Docker). Pusheada a JDis03/cbssh. PENDIENTE: testing en dispositivo real (TODO 204) antes de abrir PR (TODO 227).

features.name: SFTP Move (Cut+Paste) Hangs/Requires Cancel While Copy Works Fine
features.description: Follow-up to bug-015/feat-cbssh-copydata: the user confirmed Copy+Paste now works, but Move (Cut+Paste) still hung and had to be manually cancelled. Root cause: Copy and Move used two entirely separate code paths in SftpClient2 — the copy-data fix only touched the one Copy uses.
features.evidence:
SftpClient2.moveFile() tries rename() first (plain SSH_FXP_RENAME), then on failure fell back to `transfer.copy()` — the legacy CbsshTransfer.copy(): a serial, single-chunk-at-a-time, client-shuttled copy with NO onProgress wired through (so the UI showed only the generic indeterminate spinner with zero real feedback) and no bound on the total operation duration (only SftpDispatcher's internal 120s timeout per individual read/write request, not the whole multi-chunk loop). rename() commonly fails here specifically because plain SSH_FXP_RENAME forbids overwriting an existing destination per spec — a very common case when cutting a file to replace one already at the destination — so most real 'cut and paste to replace' operations fell straight into this slow, feedback-less fallback, which on a large file looked exactly like a hang, matching the user's report almost exactly ('copiar resultó pero mover no, tuve que cancelar'). Separately, this fallback was ALSO already broken for directory moves specifically, since CbsshTransfer.copy() always opens the path as a regular file — moveFile() never even had an isDirectory parameter to know better.

Fix: moveFile() (ISftpClient.kt + SftpClient2.kt) now takes an isDirectory: Boolean = false parameter (threaded from SftpViewModel.pasteFiles()'s entry.isDirectory, its only call site), and on rename() failure falls back to copyFileViaSsh(sourcePath, destPath, isDirectory, overwrite = true) + delete of the source (deleteDirectoryViaSsh for directories, rm for files) instead of the old CbsshTransfer.copy(). This gives Move the exact same copy-data-first / timeout-bounded-exec-fallback behavior Copy already has, and fixes the directory-move fallback as a side effect. Verified: ./init.sh BUILD SUCCESSFUL, ./gradlew assembleDebug BUILD SUCCESSFUL. No existing unit test coverage for moveFile() was found (pre-existing gap, same Docker/KnownHostRepository-mock infra blocker as bug-015/feat-cbssh-copydata's follow-up TODOs — not newly introduced by this fix). Not yet re-tested on a physical device — recommend the user retest Cut+Paste, especially replacing an already-existing destination file, to confirm the fix resolves the reported hang.

features.name: SFTP Delete Folder Silently Fails / Never Completes
features.description: User reports 'eliminar carpetas no funciona' — deleting a folder in the SFTP browser sometimes has no effect at all, with no error shown, especially when deleting several folders in quick succession.
features.evidence: Two-part fix, second part found via a real device debug log the user provided. Part 1 (root cause candidate, modernization): SftpClient2.deleteDirectoryViaSsh previously ran `rm -rf '$remotePath'` via raw SSH exec, draining only stdout with no exit-status or stderr check — if the command failed (permission denied, etc.) the error went to stderr, stdout still closed normally, and the function returned Result.success anyway, so the UI showed 'Deleted: folder' while the folder silently remained. Replaced with a pure-SFTP recursive delete (deleteDirectoryRecursive: listdir + recurse into subdirectories + remove() each file + rmdir() the emptied directory) — the standard way to delete a non-empty directory over SFTP v3, which has no native recursive-delete op. Works even for internal-sftp-only accounts with no shell, and surfaces real SFTP server errors instead of masking exec failures. Part 2 (actual root cause per device log darkssh log 2026-07-31 01:2x): user tapped delete on 3 folders within ~9 seconds of each other; the log showed only 1 of 3 deletes taking effect immediately, a second stuck for 9+ seconds with zero effect (folder still had all 6 of its original entries), and only completed after the user manually retried it — all with zero error output anywhere, because SftpViewModel.deleteEntry() only ever wrote failures to _uiState.error (a Compose StateFlow), never to DebugLogger, so nothing about a failure would show up in a shared/copied debug log even if one occurred. Root cause: deleteEntry() launches an independent, unserialized viewModelScope.launch(Dispatchers.IO) coroutine per tap, and activeClients (still keyed by hostId per the refactor-001 discard decision) is shared across taps/tabs to the same host, so several multi-request recursive-delete walks (each doing its own listdir/remove/rmdir sequence) ran concurrently against the same SftpClient2/SftpDispatcher — cbssh's SftpDispatcher itself correlates requests correctly via unique per-request IDs (ConcurrentHashMap + Mutex-guarded writes, verified by reading SftpDispatcher.kt), so this isn't a dispatcher bug, but running several independent multi-step management operations interleaved against one connection is fragile by construction. Fix: added a managementOpMutex: Mutex in SftpClient2 and wrapped the whole deleteDirectoryRecursive walk in managementOpMutex.withLock { } so concurrent delete taps queue and run one at a time instead of interleaving; also added DebugLogger.i/e logging of the actual success/failure result (there previously was only a 'starting' log line, so a stuck or failed delete left literally no trace to diagnose from a shared debug log — exactly what made part 2 hard to see in the log that led to this fix). Verified: ./init.sh BUILD SUCCESSFUL after each change. NOT yet re-verified on the user's physical device against the exact rapid-multi-delete scenario from the log — recommended the user retry deleting several folders in quick succession and confirm all of them actually disappear, and share a fresh debug log if any still don't. No automated test added (same pre-existing Docker/KnownHostRepository-mock infra gap as bug-015/226/228 — logged as a follow-up TODO). Part 3 (CORRECTS part 2's diagnosis, found via a SECOND real device log after part 2's mutex fix): the user retried and it still didn't work. The new log showed the mutex fix's actual effect: delete of a large nested folder (DarkDM) acquired the lock and a second delete (MediaFire) sat 'waiting for lock' for 28+ seconds with no completion logged for either — while unrelated ls calls on other paths kept succeeding fine throughout, proving the connection itself wasn't stuck. This revealed part 2's diagnosis was WRONG: cbssh's SftpDispatcher already correlates concurrent requests correctly (unique per-request IDs, ConcurrentHashMap + Mutex-guarded writes — re-confirmed by re-reading SftpDispatcher.kt), so there was never a real correctness bug from concurrent *independent* top-level deletes interleaving. The actual problem was that deleteDirectoryRecursive walked one entry at a time, fully sequential (list, then await each remove()/subdirectory-recursion one by one) — for a directory tree with a few dozen nested files at ~300-700ms round-trip each (per observed ls timings), that is 20-40+ seconds of pure serial network latency with zero progress feedback, indistinguishable from a hang. The managementOpMutex added in part 2 made this WORSE by fully blocking independent deletes (MediaFire) behind a single slow one (DarkDM) instead of letting them share the connection. Fix: removed managementOpMutex entirely; rewrote deleteDirectoryRecursive to delete all entries within a directory level CONCURRENTLY, bounded by a new DELETE_PIPELINE_DEPTH=8 kotlinx.coroutines.sync.Semaphore shared across the whole recursive walk (not just one level) so total in-flight requests stay bounded regardless of tree width/depth — same pipelining technique already used by TransferEngine and CbsshTransfer's parallel upload elsewhere in this file. First failure among concurrent siblings is surfaced via awaitAll() + firstOrNull{isFailure}.

features.name: TransferEngine: retries-on-timeout dead (TimeoutCancellationException swallowed as CancellationException)
features.description: Code review del transporte cbssh (SftpClient2/TransferEngine/CbsshTransfer) reveló que en los 5 catch sites de TransferEngine.kt el catch(CancellationException){throw e} venía primero, así que un timeout real de withTimeout (TimeoutCancellationException extiende CancellationException) escapaba como 'cancelación de usuario': el retry-on-timeout nunca corría, los stalls de red se reportaban como cancelados y conRetry/retryChunk/retryWriteChunk no reintentaban timeouts.
features.evidence: Agregado catch(TimeoutCancellationException) explícito ANTES de catch(CancellationException) en: download loop (retryChunk + Failed), upload loop (retryWriteChunk), withRetry (IoError retryable + backoff), retryChunk y retryWriteChunk (log + siguiente intento). La cancelación real del usuario/padre sigue re-lanzándose intacta. Verificado: ./init.sh BUILD SUCCESSFUL.

features.name: TransferEngine swallows CancellationException into TransferResult.Cancelled (breaks structured concurrency)

Verificado que SftpViewModel ya captura CancellationException en su frontera (download:759 limpia notificación; upload:1166), así que el rethrow es seguro y además arregla la notificación fantasma al cancelar downloads.
features.evidence: downloadChunksToStream y uploadInternal ahora hacen throw e en catch(CancellationException) (los finally cierran handle/stream). Los 3 compat (downloadCompat/downloadToStreamCompat/uploadCompat) mantienen el branch Cancelled como defensivo (when exhaustivo, inalcanzable). SftpClient2 ya re-lanzaba correctamente (línea 828). Tests existentes de propagación (TransferEngineRetryTest:159, RetryChunkTest:144) siguen verdes. Verificado: ./init.sh BUILD SUCCESSFUL + testDebugUnitTest OK + assembleDebug OK.

features.name: Transfer resume is broken: download truncates instead of seeking; upload skips partially without validation

API pública rota aunque la app hoy siempre pasa resumeFrom=0.

Verificado: testDebugUnitTest BUILD SUCCESSFUL + ./init.sh BUILD SUCCESSFUL + assembleDebug OK.

features.name: downloadWithProgress/uploadWithProgress hang forever (channel never closed, result discarded)

Además ignoraba parallelChunks (async sin límite, un FileInputStream por chunk). Sin callers: ni upload() ni tests la usaban.

features.name: RTT measured from async enqueue time includes coroutine-pool queueing → sawtooth, panic, 3.4MB/s on a ~7MB/s link
features.description: El dispatchTime del pipeline se tomaba al ENCOLAR el async, no al ejecutar el read/write. Con depth alto, los asyncs esperan thread del pool de coroutines compartido → el 'RTT medido' incluía esa espera → el adaptativo veía latencia subiendo → subía depth → más coroutines → más espera (auto-congestión MEDIDA). Log real 2026-08-18: depth oscilando 12<->16 toda la descarga, avgRtt 50-400ms, panic 2056ms→depth 6, y 712MB en 204s = 3408KB/s en un link de ~7MB/s.
features.evidence: Timestamp movido DENTRO del async (justo antes del sftp.read/write): PipelineRequest/PipelineWriteRequest ahora llevan Deferred<Pair<resultado, nanoTimeInicio>> y el RTT se mide desde ahí (tiempo real de red, sin cola de thread). Recalibrados los buckets: <30→12, <60→16, <120→24, else→max; maxPipelineDepth 16→32 (el motivo del downgrade a 16 — panic en depth 32 del 23-jul — era un artefacto de esta misma medición corrupta; depth 32×32KB = 1MB en vuelo llena un link de 7MB/s hasta ~150ms RTT). Tests actualizados (AdaptiveTest buckets/recovery, TransferConfigTest default 32). Verificado: testDebugUnitTest + ./init.sh BUILD SUCCESSFUL. PENDIENTE retest en dispositivo real: con el fix, la descarga de 712MB debería ir a ~7MB/s estable sin sawtooth ni panic. | Iteración 2 (log real VPN 2026-08-18): medición corregida funcionó (depth estable en 32, descarga 204s→136s = 3.4→5.1MB/s, 1 solo panic), pero el throughput seguía limitado. Causa: usuario en VPN con RTT real ~200-300ms — BDP de 7MB/s×250ms = 1.75MB en vuelo; 32×32KB=1MB no alcanzaba (throughput = depth×chunk/RTT = 4.2MB/s teórico ≈ lo medido). Fix: chunkSize 32KB→128KB (32×128KB=4MB en vuelo = ~16MB/s teórico a 250ms) + panicRttMs 2000→4000 (los picos VPN de 2-3s son transitorios; el breaker colapsaba el pipeline innecesariamente). Tests actualizados (TransferConfigTest: chunkSize 128KB, panic 4000). Verificado: testDebugUnitTest + ./init.sh + assembleDebug OK. PENDIENTE retest en dispositivo con VPN.

features.name: Upload con conexión caída intentaba fallback SCP completo sobre el socket muerto (y no llamaba markDead)
features.description: Usuario reporta que el SFTP cierra el canal en uploads varias veces. El error 'Failed to write 68 bytes' viene de KtorTcpTransport.write() = el socket TCP se cerró a mitad del upload (red inestable). Bug encontrado en SftpClient2.uploadFile: ante CUALQUIER fallo (incluido IoError de conexión) llamaba exists() y luego el fallback SCP — que intenta ssh.openSession() sobre el socket muerto y, si abriera, re-subiría el archivo COMPLETO (712MB). Además ese path devuelve el SftpResult crudo del engine (no pasa por mapResult), así que markDead() nunca se llamaba y la UI no sabía que debía reconectar.
features.evidence: uploadFile ahora corta rápido ante SftpResult.IoError: llama markDead(cause), loguea 'conexión perdida — sin fallback SCP' y devuelve Result.failure(cause). El exists()+SCP fallback queda solo para errores de servidor/protocolo con la conexión viva (su propósito original). Verificado: compileDebugKotlin + testDebugUnitTest + ./init.sh BUILD SUCCESSFUL. PENDIENTE: log del usuario en el momento exacto del fallo para confirmar si además hay un cancel involucrado (TODO 263) y evaluar auto-retry con resume.

features.name: uploadFile descartaba el motivo del fallo SFTP (log ciego)
features.description: El log del usuario solo mostraba 'SFTP upload failed, falling back to SCP' sin el motivo: uploadFile descartaba el SftpResult de error. Imposible distinguir rechazo del servidor vs conexión caída vs violación de protocolo. Bloqueaba el diagnóstico del corte al 72%.
features.evidence: Nuevo helper describeSftpFailure() cubre las 3 variantes reales de SftpResult (ServerError con statusCode+message, ProtocolError, IoError con tipo+message) y se loguea antes de decidir fallback. Verificado: compileDebugKotlin + testDebugUnitTest + ./init.sh BUILD SUCCESSFUL.

features.name: Corte de upload al 72% (=1 GiB) — hipótesis de rekey NO confirmada
features.description: Log 2026-08-30: upload de 1.475.138.004 bytes muere a los ~36s a 29MB/s = ~1.06GB. 1 GiB = 72,8% del archivo, que coincide EXACTO con SshClientConfig.rekeyBytesLimit=1_073_741_824 (default, DarkSSH nunca lo cambia). Hipótesis: el rekey a 1 GiB colisiona con el pipeline profundo (depth 24-32); cbssh bufferea paquetes durante el KEX y tira ProtocolViolationException('Too many higher-layer packets received during key exchange') al pasar MAX_REKEY_IN_FLIGHT_PACKETS=1024.
features.evidence: NO CONFIRMADA. Escrito repro en cbssh-fork (rama investigate/rekey-pipelining, NO en la rama del PR): test 'SFTP pipelined writes survive byte limit rekey' con rekeyBytesLimit=256KB, depth=32, chunk=128KB, 32MB totales contra OpenSSH 9.9p2 real (Testcontainers). PASA en 3.2s. El test de rekey que ya existía upstream es SECUENCIAL (1 request en vuelo), así que el path pipelineado no estaba cubierto — pero tampoco falla en loopback. Diferencia clave con producción: RTT ~80ms (loopback ~0ms) => mucho mayor BDP y muchos más paquetes acumulados durante la ventana del rekey. Próximo paso: nuevo log del dispositivo ya con quality-013 para leer el motivo exacto, o repro con latencia inyectada (tc netem). || LOG 2026-08-30 22:00 (con quality-013): falla en offset 1072168960 = chunk 8180 de 8192, o sea a 12 chunks (1,5 MiB) EXACTOS de 1 GiB con 24 en vuelo => el corte esta en el borde del rekey, ya no es coincidencia. Ademas la reconexion loguea kex=mlkem768x25519-sha256 [post-quantum]: el rekey es ML-KEM768, con mensajes de KEX mucho mas grandes que un DH clasico, lo que NO estaba replicado en el repro de loopback. Falta el motivo que devuelve cbssh: lo tapaba TransferEngine (arreglado en quality-014).

features.name: TransferEngine descartaba la causa real del fallo de escritura
features.description: El log del dispositivo con quality-013 llegó hasta 'IoError IOException: Write failed at offset 1072168960 after retries', pero ese mensaje lo genera el propio TransferEngine (linea 907) y NO dice qué devolvió cbssh. retryWriteChunk() devolvía Boolean y tiraba a la basura tanto el SftpResult no-Success como las excepciones, así que era imposible saber si el rekey produce un ProtocolError, un IoError de socket o timeouts.
features.evidence: retryWriteChunk ahora devuelve String? (null=exito, o descripcion de la ULTIMA causa) y el IOException final incluye '— última causa: <detalle>'. Nuevo helper describeFailure(). Los 3 call sites migrados preservando la semantica de totalRetries (se incrementa solo si el reintento tuvo exito). Verificado: compileDebugKotlin + testDebugUnitTest + ./init.sh BUILD SUCCESSFUL.

features.name: Los logs mostraban solo el wrapper del error, no la causa anidada
features.description: cbssh envuelve el error real en TransportException('Failed to write N bytes', e) dentro de KtorTcpTransport.write(). describeFailure/describeSftpFailure imprimian solo el primer nivel, ocultando si abajo habia un Broken pipe, un Connection reset o una CancellationException.
features.evidence: Ambos helpers ahora recorren la cadena de causas (hasta 5 niveles, unidas con ' ← '). Verificado: compileDebugKotlin + testDebugUnitTest + ./init.sh BUILD SUCCESSFUL.

features.name: Experimento decisivo: la falla sigue al umbral de rekey del cliente (mi teoría del rekey simultáneo quedó REFUTADA)
features.description: CAUSA RAIZ. Los logs de sshd del propio servidor (es la misma maquina de desarrollo, journalctl -u sshd) muestran 'rekey out/in after 134217728 blocks' = 134217728 x 8 bytes = 1 GiB exacto. cbssh trae rekeyBytesLimit = 1_073_741_824 (1 GiB) por default. Ambos extremos disparaban SSH_MSG_KEXINIT en el mismo byte => rekey simultaneo. cbssh, ante un KEXINIT entrante con kex ya en progreso, lanza ProtocolViolationException(responseSent=true), que manda DISCONNECT y cierra la conexion; por eso el write al socket fallaba RAPIDO (~2s) en vez de agotar el operationTimeoutMs de 60s, y siempre en el chunk 8180-8181 de 8192.
features.evidence: REFUTADA la hipótesis del rekey simultáneo. Al bajar rekeyBytesLimit a 512 MiB el upload no se arregló: murió en offset 535822336 = chunk 4088 de 4096, o sea pegado a los 512 MiB nuevos (antes moría en el chunk 8180/8192 = 1 GiB, el default). La falla SIGUE al umbral configurado en el cliente => la rompe el rekey que inicia cbssh, sin importar el límite del servidor; si fuera simultaneidad, escalonar lo habría evitado. Gracias a quality-015 se vio además la causa de fondo: 'ClosedWriteChannelException: Connection reset by peer' (RST del servidor). Efecto colateral: 512 MiB EMPEORABA la situación (fallaba antes), revertido en quality-017. Repros en loopback que NO reproducen (rama investigate/rekey-pipelining del fork): pipelineado depth 32 (3.2s) y pipelineado con kex post-cuántico mlkem768x25519-sha256, rekey cada 4MB, 64MB (1.6s) — ambos PASAN, así que ML-KEM también queda descartado como variable. Queda la latencia/BDP real (80-300ms) como única variable sin replicar.

features.name: Experimento: el rekey del SERVIDOR también rompe la transferencia (rompe cualquier rekey)
features.description: Como la falla sigue al umbral de rekey del cliente (quality-016), y el fix de fondo es en cbssh, se lleva rekeyBytesLimit a 8 GiB para que el cliente no dispare un rekey en medio de un upload normal. Revierte el 512 MiB, que empeoraba las cosas.
features.evidence: Resultado del experimento: con rekeyBytesLimit del cliente en 8 GiB el upload igual murió en offset 1072693248 = chunk 8184 de 8192, o sea 1 GiB exacto — que es donde rekeya el SERVIDOR ('rekey out after 134217728 blocks'), no el cliente. Conclusión: rompe CUALQUIER rekey, también el entrante, así que el fix en cbssh debe cubrir los dos sentidos. El error además cambió a 'ClosedReceiveChannelException: Channel was closed' (antes 'Connection reset by peer'), o sea ahora se cae por el lado de LECTURA. Se mantiene el umbral en 8 GiB porque evita al menos el rekey propio del cliente. Repro nuevo en el fork (rama investigate/rekey-pipelining): 'SFTP pipelined writes survive SERVER-initiated rekey' — RekeyLimit 4M en el sshd del contenedor vía SIGHUP, cliente con rekey desactivado, 64MB pipelineados depth 32, CON assert de no-vacuidad que verifica en los logs del servidor que hubo rekeys reales: PASA (3.7s). Loopback sigue sin reproducir.

features.name: DarkSSH ejecutaba un jar cbssh antiguo sin el gate de paquetes durante rekey
features.description: La causa final fue una divergencia source/binario. El source actual de cbssh contiene OutboundPacketController, que pausa SSH_MSG_CHANNEL_DATA durante KEX y pasa los repros con OpenSSH 10.5p1, ML-KEM768, rekey iniciado por cliente/servidor y 80 ms de netem. El jar 0.3.3-SNAPSHOT realmente cargado por DarkSSH no contenía SshConnection$OutboundPacketController.class: seguía enviando SFTP durante el rekey, por lo que OpenSSH cortaba la conexión en su umbral de 1 GiB. sshj no fallaba porque sí implementa correctamente esa pausa.
features.evidence: El jar anterior (~/.m2/.../0.3.3-SNAPSHOT) no contenía OutboundPacketController; el gate fue agregado en cbssh commit d23e6e6. Se creó la rama build/0.3.3-kotlin-2.3-rekey-fix desde el source actual, conservando versión 0.3.3-SNAPSHOT y Kotlin 2.3.21 para compatibilidad con Hilt. Publicado a Maven Local: el jar nuevo sí contiene SshConnection$OutboundPacketController.class. DarkSSH recompiló con --refresh-dependencies: compileDebugKotlin + testDebugUnitTest + ./init.sh BUILD SUCCESSFUL. Falta validar en dispositivo que el upload de 1.4 GB cruza el rekey de 1 GiB.

features.name: Abrir archivos SFTP con aplicaciones Android
features.description: Al tocar un archivo remoto, descargarlo temporalmente y mostrar el selector de Android 'Open with', como un file manager. La acción Download sigue guardando una copia permanente en Downloads.
features.evidence: Toque corto de archivo llama requestOpenFile: descarga a un directorio UUID único bajo cacheDir/sftp-open/<hostId>, reutiliza progreso/cancelación, elimina parciales en NonCancellable al fallar/cancelar y emite un evento one-shot. La decisión final de cancelación se serializa en Main para impedir abrir tras un cancel tardío. SftpScreen usa un ViewModel separado por host y consume eventos solo con pestaña activa y lifecycle RESUMED; comparte con FileProvider y usa ACTION_VIEW + Intent.createChooser. .md/.markdown usan text/markdown y otros formatos se resuelven por extensión. El menú Download conserva la descarga permanente. La caché exitosa se poda tras 24h y el canal de notificación está protegido para API 24/25. 6 tests cubren nombres seguros, MIME y poda. Verificado: test específico, testDebugUnitTest y ./init.sh BUILD SUCCESSFUL. lintDebug sigue bloqueado por 42 errores preexistentes; ninguno nuevo atribuible a esta feature. Pendiente smoke test del chooser en dispositivo.

features.name: Atajos Ctrl+0 a Ctrl+9 distinguibles en SSH
features.description: Evitar la conversión ASCII heredada donde Ctrl+1 se volvía '1', Ctrl+2 NUL y Ctrl+3 Escape, enviando Ctrl+0 a Ctrl+9 como secuencias CSI-u explícitas al terminal remoto.
features.evidence: KeyHandler produce ESC[48;5u hasta ESC[57;5u para Ctrl+0 a Ctrl+9, incluyendo keypad; TerminalView las escribe antes del fallback ASCII, sin duplicar eventos. Ctrl con Shift/Alt y teclas no numéricas conservan la compatibilidad heredada. KeyHandlerControlDigitTest cubre los 10 dígitos de fila, keypad 0/5/9 y casos no aplicables. Verificado: test específico y ./init.sh BUILD SUCCESSFUL. Pendiente smoke test en dispositivo con la TUI remota que consume CSI-u.
